sections.heading: How things work here
rules: Your country, legal entity and role decide which policies apply to you. This page shows only those.
Requests (leave, expenses, letters, exits) go to the person above you in the reporting line.
If nobody is above you (the CEO), your time off is recorded without approval.
Ask HR through the Helpdesk if a rule is unclear.

sections.heading: Where to find things
rules: Leave, holidays, timesheets and pay sit under Time & pay.
Letters and your own documents sit under Documents & letters.
Concerns can be raised in confidence under Raise a concern.

sections.heading: Expected behaviour
rules: Treat colleagues with respect. Harassment and discrimination are not tolerated.
Declare conflicts of interest to your manager and HR.
Use company systems and data only for work.

sections.heading: Raising a concern
rules: Raise concerns under Me → Raise a concern. HR handles them in confidence.
Retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith is a conduct breach.

sections.heading: Allowance
rules: Work from home: 8 days a year.
Emergency work from home: 3 days a year.

sections.heading: How to apply
rules: Apply under Leave & holidays, like any other leave type.
Approval goes up your reporting line.
Keep your usual working hours and stay reachable.

sections.heading: Programs
rules: Programs assigned to you appear under Learning.
Progress is recorded module by module.
Once a program is marked complete it can't be reopened.

sections.heading: Who can see what
rules: Your personal data: you, HR, and people above you in your reporting line.
Your pay and payslips: you and Compensation only.
Managers do not see individual pay.

sections.heading: Account security
rules: You are signed out after 30 minutes without activity.
Editing your own profile needs two-step verification.
Never share your password or one-time codes.
You can see and request your data under Me → Privacy.

sections.heading: What you approve
rules: You decide requests from people below you in the reporting line, never your own.
Sick leave can't be applied in advance; past-dated leave older than 7 days needs your prior permission (valid 30 days).
Timesheets above 9 hours a day are refused.
Pay stays restricted: you don't see your team's salaries.

sections.heading: Probation
rules: Reviews come due 60 days before probation ends.
Probation can be extended at most 2 times, 1 to 3 months each.
HR finalises the manager's recommendation.

sections.heading: Key terms
rules: Notice to end the engagement: 7 days.
Employee benefit plans don't apply to contractors.

sections.heading: Your yearly entitlement
rules: Privilege leave: 18 days a year (accrues monthly; up to 10 days carry over).
Casual leave: 6 days a year.
Sick leave: 10 days a year.

sections.heading: Everyone also gets

Emergency work from home: 3 days a year.
Bereavement leave: 3 days a year.

Comp-off: earned only by working on a weekly off or holiday; use it within 90 days.

sections.heading: Applying
rules: Sick leave can't be applied in advance.
Past-dated leave older than 7 days needs prior permission from your manager (valid 30 days).
Approval goes up your reporting line. The CEO's time off is recorded with no approval.

sections.heading: Encashment
